name: Antidepressants / anxiety meds

lead: Antidepressants are prescription drugs used mainly for major depressive disorder and also for anxiety disorders such as generalized and social anxiety, panic disorder, OCD and PTSD. In the scene they come up as aids for anxiety or low mood that hold back confidence.

The chain: lower anxiety or low mood, easier social interaction, a more relaxed, confident presence. They are prescribed for mental-health conditions, not appearance, and no study tests them for looksmaxxing concerns. Meta-analyses find they beat placebo in depression by a modest margin; for anxiety disorders the effect size is about 0.3.

paras: They are prescribed by a clinician after assessment and taken as a regular daily course, often alongside talk therapy. Most act on serotonin, sometimes with norepinephrine, and effects build over weeks. Main classes include SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics and MAOIs.

Reported effects include sexual dysfunction, weight change and emotional blunting. An FDA warning covers suicidal thinking in people under 25, and stopping suddenly can cause discontinuation symptoms. Prescription only.

angle.text: Prescription antidepressants and anxiety medicines come up in the scene as aids for social anxiety and low mood that can hold back confidence, making interaction easier and presence more relaxed. They are prescribed for mental-health conditions rather than appearance.

lead: Antidepressants are prescription drugs used mainly for major depressive disorder and also for anxiety disorders such as generalized and social anxiety, panic disorder, OCD and PTSD. Main classes include SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics and MAOIs.[1]

Meta-analyses find they outperform placebo in depression by a modest margin; for anxiety disorders the drug-placebo effect size is about 0.3.[1] They are not appearance treatments and no study tests them for looksmaxxing-related concerns. Common adverse effects include sexual dysfunction, weight change and emotional blunting.[1]
infobox: SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, MAOIs and others

paras: Medical uses include depression, anxiety disorders, chronic pain and some eating disorders.[1] Some drugs hold specific approvals; paroxetine is approved for social anxiety and PTSD.[1]
Effects over placebo are modest, around 30 to 50 percent of people do not respond to a given drug, and critics argue trial design and publication bias inflate benefit.[1]

Common effects include dry mouth, weight changes, dizziness, headaches, akathisia, sexual dysfunction and emotional blunting.[1] An FDA warning describes increased suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults, highest in the first one to two months.[1] Roughly 20 to 50 percent who stop suddenly report discontinuation symptoms.[1]

No studies found for looks-related anxiety. Registered trials of the drug class address general conditions, such as an antidepressant safety study in young people with anxiety, depressive and obsessive-compulsive disorders (n=569),[2] and a trial comparing sertraline with virtual-reality exposure for social anxiety disorder.[3]
